children: The Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) has mandated a syndicate of banks to arrange a new benchmark-sized five-year USD sukuk under its $25 billion Trust Certificate Issuance Programme.

IPTs are set in the area of 50bps over the five-year US SOFR mid-swap rate, with investor orders being gathered ahead of an expected launch on September 2, subject to market conditions. The profit rate will be fixed and paid semi-annually.

The Saudi-headquartered lender has appointed Bank of China, Barclays, BMO Capital Markets, China International Capital Corporation (CICC), Goldman Sachs International, HSBC, ICBC, KFH Capital, Natixis and Societe Generale as joint lead managers and bookrunners for the Regulation S issuance. HSBC is acting as the billing and delivery bank for the transaction.
The certificates are expected to carry ratings of Aaa/AAA/AAA from Moody's, S&P and Fitch, in line with the obligor ratings.
The issuance will be structured as a senior unsecured sukuk and will be listed on the International Securities Market of the London Stock Exchange, Euronext Dublin and Nasdaq Dubai.
(Writing by Ahmad Mousa; editing by Bindu Rai)

title: Islamic Development Bank mandates 5-year USD benchmark sukuk
